chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Among the signs of wretchedness are the stillness of the eye, the hardness of the heart, the intensity of greed in seeking the world, and persistence in sin.'

key_terms.الشَّقَاءِ: Wretchedness or misery, the opposite of felicity (sa'ādah)
key_terms.الْإِصْرَارُ: Persistence or stubbornness in continuing an action, specifically sin
key_terms.جُمُودُ الْعَيْنِ: Stillness or lack of depth/reflection in the eye, indicating superficiality
key_terms.قَسْوَةُ الْقَلْبِ: Hardness of the heart, indicating insensitivity to divine signs and moral truths

ai.seo_question: What are the four signs of spiritual wretchedness in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi’s chapter on the roots of disbelief, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links these four traits to the concept of *al-shaqā'ah* (wretchedness), presenting them as the internal precursors to spiritual ruin. This narration is often cited by Shia scholars to illustrate how external behaviors stem from an internal state of spiritual blindness and stubbornness, mirroring the condition of those who reject divine guidance despite clear signs.
